1.he: וּמַרְאֵה עֵינַיו עַל שֵׂכֶל רַעְיוֹנָיו הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל
1.note: "Going about as a talebearer" (Lev 19:16, Prov 11:13) is turned to a good sense: his appearance gave away the wisdom inside him.

2.note: From Prov 30:27, of the locusts that "go forth in ranks" (חֹצֵץ). Here it may mean that the hawk goes forth dividing the air; the sense is not certain. The word rhymes with נֵץ "hawk" and מִתְנוֹצֵץ "glittering".

3.note: A pun on 1 Sam 26:20: קוֹרֵא is both "one who calls out" and the partridge (קֹרֵא) that is hunted on the mountains.

4.note: From Nah 2:5 יִשְׁתַּקְשְׁקוּן (the chariots "rush to and fro"); here of the doe's playful running with her young.

5.note: Literally "and came from an entry" (compare Ezek 46:8-9). Perhaps: he came in by the way into the cave. The sense is not certain.

6.note: Hos 11:10. In Hosea מִיָּם means "from the west" (from the sea); here the "children" are the young of the gazelles.

7.note: "Like lions" (כִּלְבָאִים) sounds almost the same as כְּלָבִים "hounds".
